Class GenericWidgetElement<T extends Widget>

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.toolkit.element.StyledElement<GenericWidgetElement<T>>
dev.tamboui.toolkit.elements.GenericWidgetElement<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of the wrapped widget
All Implemented Interfaces:
Styleable, Element
public final class GenericWidgetElement<T extends Widget> extends StyledElement<GenericWidgetElement<T>>
A generic element that wraps any Widget and exposes it as a StyledElement.

This is useful when you need to use a widget that doesn't have a dedicated element wrapper, allowing it to participate in the toolkit's styling and layout system.

When to Use

  • You have a custom or third-party widget without a dedicated toolkit element
  • You need quick integration of a widget into the toolkit DSL
  • You want to apply layout constraints, CSS classes, or event handlers to a widget

Example Usage

// Wrap any widget
GenericWidgetElement.of(someWidget)
    .fg(Color.RED)
    .addClass("custom-class")
    .fill()

// Or use the Toolkit DSL
import static dev.tamboui.toolkit.Toolkit.*;
widget(someWidget).bold()

Limitations

  • Styling does not propagate: Styles set on this element (colors, modifiers) do not affect the widget's internal rendering. The widget renders directly to the buffer using its own styling logic.
  • No CSS child selectors: This element has no sub-components that can be styled via CSS child selectors.
  • No preferred size: This element does not implement preferredWidth() or preferredHeight() since the wrapped widget's size requirements are unknown.

For full styling support, consider creating a dedicated element wrapper for the specific widget type.

    • preferredSize

      public Size preferredSize(int availableWidth, int availableHeight, RenderContext context)
      Description copied from interface: Element
      Returns the preferred size of this element.

      The availableWidth/Height parameters allow elements to adapt their dimensions based on constraints. Use -1 for unconstrained.

      Common patterns:

      • Text elements: height depends on width (text wrapping)
      • Aspect-ratio elements: both dimensions interrelated
      • Fixed elements: ignore available dimensions

      Return value semantics:

      • Positive values = known size (use as constraint)
      • Zero = explicitly zero-sized (element should collapse)
      • Negative (-1) = unknown size (element should fill available space)
      Parameters:
      availableWidth - the available width in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      availableHeight - the available height in cells, or -1 if unconstrained
      context - the render context for CSS resolution, may be null
      Returns:
      the preferred size
